slides.title: 20 to 30 Minutes That Replace Months of Visits
bullets: A congress KOL meeting is often the year's densest interaction with that person
It packs into 20 to 30 minutes what field visits would take months to cover
That density demands preparation different from an ordinary field visit

slides.title: Define the Specific Purpose First
bullets: Is this an insight-exploration conversation on a new area?
Is it a chance to present and discuss recent product data?
Is it a first contact to gauge interest in a research collaboration?
Or is it maintenance of an already consolidated relationship?
Each purpose demands a different structure, per Module 4 exchange principles

slides.title: Go Straight to the Essential
bullets: Interruptions and packed agendas are the norm at a congress
Open with a question genuinely relevant to the KOL, ideally tied to their own recent work
Listen actively and leave deliberate space for their perspective
Never let the company message monopolize the limited time

slides.title: Connect to What's Happening Right Now
bullets: The KOL likely just left, or is heading to, a session with new data
A prepared MSL links the conversation to what the congress is discussing that moment
This shows genuine immersion, not a fixed company agenda

slides.title: Document Immediately, Before Memory Fades
bullets: Capture key points and insights right after, or as soon as possible
Follow the insight-capture framework from Module 5
Waiting until the end of the congress risks losing nuance
It also risks mixing up details between different interlocutors

takeaway.title: Congress KOL meetings pack a year's worth of relationship value into minutes
bullets: A clear purpose defined beforehand shapes how the conversation runs
Genuine, real-time engagement beats reciting a fixed agenda
Immediate documentation is what keeps that value from being lost
